definition: An event has no primary when none of its hit rows has is_secondary = 0, the producer's primary-particle tag. Each bar is the fraction of the selected events that have none, an event being the unit.
notes: An event has no primary when none of its hit rows has is_secondary = 0, the producer's primary-particle tag. Each bar is the fraction of the selected events that have none, an event being the unit. Bars start at zero.

Whiskers are 95% Wilson score intervals of the fraction, events being the independent units. The Wald interval is not used: it collapses at zero events and leaves [0, 1] at small N. 8 bins with N < 20 have a correspondingly wide interval.
Bins are the producer's integer momentum bin, closed on the left, labelled with the momenta found in them.
The count distribution is exact, not an estimate: the number of primary-tagged hit rows per event, 0 to 9, and a last bucket of 10 or more.

Reference measurement on the electron file (100,000 events, not this selection): 73.83% of events hold no primary-tagged hit row, rising from 64% in momentum bin 1 to 80% in bin 18; the roadmap had expected 25–27%.
